sections.h2: Where does Upson County fit in west central Georgia?
sections.html:
Upson County lies in west central Georgia, roughly the same distance from Atlanta, Macon and Columbus. The state legislature established it on December 15, 1824, on land the Creek gave up in the Treaty of Indian Springs of 1821, and many early settlers arrived through the land lottery. It was Georgia's fifty-ninth county, named for a lawyer who had died only four months before.

Thomaston is the county seat. The Rock and Yatesville are the other incorporated places. The county reports 326 square miles of land and 592 miles of roads. The Flint River runs unimpeded through the area, and Sprewell Bluff Park, which the county has managed since January 2013, offers trails, cabins, RV sites and an overlook.

Textile mills turned Thomaston into a social and cultural center in the nineteenth century, according to the county's history page, though cotton's hold on the economy had faded by 1900. Houses range from mill-era homes in town to timber and farm tracts outside it.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show for Upson County?
sections.html:
Upson had 28,500 residents in the July 2025 estimate, up 2.9% from 2020. About 61.0% of housing units are owner-occupied, and the median owner-occupied home is worth $168,700.

Residents 65 and over make up 20.8% of the population, and 92.8% lived in the same house the year before. The county assessors maintain more than 15,000 real property parcels and about 1,400 personal property accounts, so the digest is small enough that each office knows its parcels well.

sections.h2: Which Upson County office should I call?
sections.html:
Both offices are in the same building, at 305 South Hightower Street in Thomaston. Which you need depends on whether your question is about money owed or about value.

  • Tax commissioner, Suite D-120, (706) 647-8931, mailing address P.O. Box 409: billing, collection, tags and the tax payoff for a sale.
  • Tax assessors, Suite D-180, (706) 647-8176, mailing address P.O. Box 508, open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.: values, returns, exemptions and appeals.
  • Clerk of Superior Court, 116 W. Main Street: copies of your warranty deed.

The tax commissioner is an independently elected office and does not report to the assessors or to the county commissioners. Tax statements go to the homeowner, never to the mortgage company, though the office sends a data file to lenders on record. If your lender changed recently, forward the bill yourself.

sections.h2: When do Upson County bills arrive and when are they due?
sections.html:
Real and personal property statements are mailed by September 15, and the county FAQ says the due date is typically around November 15. Mobile and manufactured home statements are mailed by January 30 and the tax is due April 1.

The county also posted a 2026 notice of property tax increase: a tentatively adopted county rate of 8.244 mills, up 0.391 mills, with public hearings held on August 26 and September 8, 2026. The notice listed the rate that would apply without the increase as no more than 7.853 mills. Check your own bill for the final rate, since the school board and the city set separate ones.

  • Assessed value is 40% of fair market value.
  • Millage is set by the school board, the county commissioners and the City of Thomaston.
  • Postmarks from the U.S. Postal Service count; meter postmarks do not.

sections.h2: What do late Upson County payments cost?
sections.html:
Late balances carry monthly interest at the January prime rate plus 3%. A 5% penalty lands 120 days after the due date, and another 5% follows every 120 days until the penalty reaches 20%.

The tax commissioner accepts partial payments for legitimate hardship, but only if you call before the due date to set up an arrangement, and interest and penalties keep running on what remains. When a bill sits unpaid, the office mails a 30-day notice of intent before filing a FIFA lien on the General Execution Docket. Tax unpaid more than 90 days after the due date can be liened, and credit bureaus can read those public records. Paying the tax, fees, penalties and interest cancels the lien. The office does not sell liens over the counter.

sections.h2: How do I contest an Upson County assessment?
sections.html:
You have 45 days from the date on the notice to file. The appeal can rest on taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption, and it must be written and filed first with the Board of Assessors, naming the method of appeal you choose.

The assessors' page also posts field review notices that allow representatives with identification to enter property during business hours to confirm value. Homestead applications go to the assessors between January 1 and March 31 and must arrive by April 1. You must own and live in the house on January 1, and you do not need to reapply while you stay in the same house with no deed change. Call (706) 647-8176 for the exemption amounts that apply to your parcel.

sections.h2: What should an Upson County seller do about the tax bill?
sections.html:
Request a written payoff from the tax commissioner before closing and make sure the closing agent pays it from the proceeds. Because the bill follows the January 1 owner, a seller who closes in the fall should confirm who covers the current year on the settlement statement.

If you inherited the house or rented it out, ask the office for the status of every year, including any FIFA on file. A tax lien cancels only when the full amount is paid, so a buyer's title company will want the account clear. Houses with back taxes, repair needs or tenants still sell, since a cash purchase can pay old balances at closing and leave you with the remainder.

faqs.q: What is the Upson County tax commissioner's phone number?
faqs.a: It is (706) 647-8931. The office is at 305 South Hightower Street, Suite D-120, Thomaston.

faqs.q: What is the due date for Upson County property tax?
faqs.a: The county FAQ says the due date is typically around November 15. Mobile and manufactured homes are due April 1.

faqs.q: How big is the penalty for paying late in Upson County?
faqs.a: A 5% penalty applies 120 days after the due date and repeats every 120 days up to 20%, plus monthly interest at prime plus 3%.

faqs.q: How long can I appeal an Upson County value?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the notice date. File in writing with the Board of Assessors and state which appeal method you want.

faqs.q: Does the county send my bill to my mortgage company?
faqs.a: No. Statements go to the homeowner. The office sends lenders a data file, but you are responsible for forwarding your bill if needed.
